I went to Reddit to participate in specialized discussions of a various sort and replaced all of the previous (dying) forums that I used to frequent. One part of forum culture that has always been a favorite of mine is the community aspect and the feeling that one is actually making friends with other people.

On Reddit, I've never experienced that feeling. The crowd is so big and there's nothing separating people except for a simple username, so many users go unnoticed and friends really aren't made. The tagging feature of RES was only a temporary fix, but rather than developing a friendship, the tagging feature was more of stereotyping the type a user a person was based on a previous post.

I've always had illusions of grandeur, mostly that I'd become a "famous" user. But that never happened on Reddit. Nobody ever acknowledged me and friendly banter was a minimal. People care more about making meme references in the right places and cultivating karma than actually participate in a community.

I think our "follow/friend" feature will help change that. Random comments to random people are okay, but being able to "follow/friend" someone (with their permission perhaps) would help the same people interact more. Every time you submit something, I would see it on my frontpage (favorite users/friends section) and be able to dig right in :) We'll definitely implement this at some point.
That would definitely be a great feature!
